name: dispatch_refill
fields: launch.dispatch slot_free_to_entry_ns / serial_ns_per_cta / first_wave_interval_ns (how the engine applies them; values only if a rule needs a constant that is not installed)
ownership: gpu-shared (full-GPU loop): the refill of CTA slots in launches with more CTAs than slots. A single-cluster job has one cluster and no refill.
question: In a launch with more CTAs than slots, how long does a CTA slot stay empty between the exit of one CTA and the first instruction of the next, as a function of the CTA residency, of how many slots the SM has, of how synchronised the exits are, and of what the CTAs do while resident (spin, sleep, wait for cold global memory)?
why: FIF-RMSNORM-C03 (B300 full GPU, sim/ncu 0.69) was handed over as a cold-DRAM first-access gap: the hardware share of samples waiting for the cp.async data (37.6 %) was converted to cycles per CTA with the assumption that all 2368 slots are always occupied (2140 cycles against 1090 simulated). ncu's own per-warp counters contradict that assumption: sum over reasons of smsp__average_warp_latency_issue_stalled_<reason>.ratio (cycles per launched warp; the `selected` term equals inst_executed / warps exactly) is 2823-3122 cycles for the four profiled launches of the kernel, of which long_scoreboard 1203-1476 (LDS.128 holds 242 of the 289 long-scoreboard samples -> 1007-1236 cycles against 1089 simulated). With 8192 CTAs, 2368 slots and 17.8-18.1 k active cycles per SM that is a slot fill of 0.56-0.60; the r22 simulation of the same case has a mean first-to-last-issue residency of 3320 cycles and a fill of 0.87. The gap of the case is therefore in how full the slots are, not in the wait for the data. For single-wave kernels (grid = SM count) the same counter sum is 0.95-1.00 of sm__cycles_active.avg, which is what the reading of the counters as residency predicts.
data_already_seen: $A/fg-line-cold/notes/hw-fill-{bw,hp}.tsv (tools/hw_fill_all.py over every profiled launch of $A/fg-fa3/hwmet, $A/fg-line-mem/hwmet, $A/fg-fix5/r1/pc; 304 + 202 launches with more than two waves): with 16 CTAs of 4 warps per SM the slot period minus the residency is about 2000-2300 cycles for residencies below 500 (both devices; the 1.01 / 1.14 cycles per CTA GPU-wide ceiling), 1000-1250 for residencies 1300-6000 at 3-12 waves, 590-700 at 14-36 waves on B300, 900-1600 on H100; FIF-RMSNORM-C03 2265. The installed rule's 160 / 175 ns (324 / 306 cycles) per refill is below all of them.

$A/microbench/dispatch/b300-r41/run-a/tput.c{4,16}.w8.txt re-read per SM (tools/dispatch_persm.py): the first wave of an SM enters serially, one CTA every 26 cycles (16 CTAs take about 400 cycles; the model's first-wave reading resolved only 32 ns ticks); after the first wave the CTA index order sweeps the SMs in the first wave's SM order and an SM receives at most one CTA per sweep; with 4 slots per SM the exit -> entry gaps of the four slots of one SM are 290 / 295 / 350 / 428 cycles.

the present engine rule read from cpp/core/simulator.cpp: a dispatch event fills every slot released so far, also slots released less than slot_free_to_entry ago; with staggered exits the simulated gap is a few cycles (model.py predict, jitter cells).
probe: tools/microbench/dispatch_refill/probe/refill.cu: one kernel, grid = sm_count x occ x waves, CTAs of <threads> threads; thread 0 records %smid, %warpid, clock64 and %globaltimer at the CTA's first instruction and after a final __syncthreads; the CTA stays resident for <hold> SM cycles from its own first clock read. Hold kinds: spin (all threads loop on clock64), sleep (all threads loop on nanosleep.u32 64), ldg (each thread first loads 16 B of its own from a buffer evicted from L2 by a 512 MiB memset before the launch; the hold length depends on the loaded zero), cpasync (the same 16 B through cp.async.cg into shared memory, wait_group 0, read back). --jitter J: hold x (1 +- J / 1000) uniform by a hash of the CTA index. --occ 0: the device's own occupancy (128 threads: 16 CTAs per SM by warps; 256: 8; 512: 4; 32: the per-SM CTA limit), shared request 32 + threads x 16 B; --occ N: the dynamic shared request is sized so that exactly N CTAs fit. The cp.async code is in the binary in every mode (one kernel).

cells.names: <mode>.t<threads>.o<occ request>.w<waves>.h<hold>.j<jitter permille>; the list is CELLS in model.py and the same list in run.sh
cells.B staggered exits: spin.t128.o0 jitter 300: hold 3000 waves 4 and 12, hold 6000 waves 12
cells.C slots and warps per CTA: hold 3000 waves 12: t128.o4, t128.o8 (shared-memory limited), t256.o0, t512.o0, t32.o0
cells.D what the CTA does: sleep.t128.o0 hold 3000 waves 4 and 12; ldg and cpasync t128.o0 hold 3000 waves 4 and 12, hold 0 waves 4
cells.E method check: spin.t128.o0.w4.h3000.j0 and cpasync.t128.o0.w4.h3000.j0, 3 launches each, under ncu --cache-control all --replay-mode kernel with the stall-latency counters, sm__cycles_active.{max,avg}, smsp__inst_executed.sum

derivation: model.py cells <run dir>: per launch R, occupancy, first-wave step, FIFO slot gap per refill (k-th refill entry of an SM minus that SM's k-th exit) overall / by generation / by the number of free slots after the exit, GPU-wide span (per-SM clocks aligned by the globaltimer), fill, CTAs per sweep, refill rate; replay of M0 and M1 on the measured residencies in CTA-index order with the installed constants of the device (b300 160 ns / 0.513613 ns, h100 174.924 ns / 0.617 ns, converted with the run's measured cycles per ns and truncated to whole cycles as the engine does). Medians over launches 1-4. model.py ncu: counter sum against the in-kernel residency.

models_declared_before_data.M0: the engine today: first wave at cycle 0; a slot is released at the CTA's exit; a dispatch event `slot` cycles after a release fills every slot released by then in SM order; consecutive entries >= `serial` apart GPU-wide.
models_declared_before_data.M1: M0 with the leaf's literal meaning: a slot can be refilled only `slot` cycles after its own release. No new constant.
models_declared_before_data.predictions (model.py predict, nominal R: constant holds: M0 = M1; mean gap 718 (waves 4) / 432 (waves 12) for hold >= 3000, generation 2 1508, later generations 324; hold 1500: 894 / 672; hold 800: 1361 / 1308; hold 0: 1894 / 2035 (the serial ceiling). Jitter 300: M0 208 / 60 (hold 3000, waves 4 / 12) and 8 (hold 6000), later generations 4-8 cycles; M1 423 / 352 and 324. occ 4 / 8: 351 / 378; t32 (32 slots): 1568. sleep = spin. h100 at 1.755: slot 306, the same pattern (658 / 402, jitter M0 159 / 46 / 7, M1 360 / 321 / 306).
models_declared_before_data.expectation: from the counters already seen I expect both models to under-predict the gap of the constant-hold cells of generation 3 and later (about 600-1100 measured against 324) unless the excess of the real kernels comes from their memory activity (cells D against A decide), and M0 to fail the jitter cells by a large factor.

reading.usable cell: no OCCMISMATCH, no negative gap, span spread over launches 1-4 <= 5 %.
reading.method check (E): per profiled launch, counter sum / in-kernel mean R within 0.90-1.15 (the counters also cover launch-to-first-instruction and last-record-to-exit) -> the counter sum is accepted as residency and the fill numbers of the real kernels stand. Outside -> the fill attribution is not supported by this check; report both numbers and stop.
reading.a model holds for a cell: span within 5 % and mean gap within max(15 %, 60 cycles) of the replay on the measured residencies.
reading.M0 / M1: judged on all usable spin cells with 16 slots (A, B). M1 holds and M0 fails B -> the engine's early refill is a defect, M1 replaces it, no leaf changes. Both hold -> nothing to change in dispatch; the fill gap of the real kernels is not reproduced by hold kernels and cells D say whether memory activity is the difference. Both fail -> stage 2.
reading.stage 2: candidates are written as an addendum after reading this run (post hoc, said so), each with the cells its constants come from; they are judged with the same criterion on the remaining cells of this run and on a second run with holds 2200 / 4500 / 9000, jitter 150, waves 6, whose predictions are written before it. A candidate that needs a constant not in the tree installs it as experimental with source dispatch_refill.<device>.<run>.
reading.D against A: mean gap of the ldg / cpasync / sleep cell within 15 % of the spin cell replayed at the same measured residency distribution (M1 or the stage-2 rule) -> the refill does not depend on what the CTA does. Otherwise the dependence is reported with its sign and size; if it is on the memory cells, stop and report before any engine change (it may belong to the shared memory path).
reading.C: reported; a stage-2 candidate has to cover the 4 / 8 / 32-slot cells or name them as open.

install: engine rule in cpp/core/simulator.cpp + cpp/core/dispatch.*; CTest fixture for the rule (staggered exits: every refill >= slot after its own release; simultaneous exits: serial spacing); new constants only through schema 24 fields with ids after 3 (0-3 used: first_wave_interval_ns, slot_free_to_entry_ns, enabled, serial_ns_per_cta); tree build && tree validate --strict; CTest; pytest; two-architecture full-GPU regression reported against $A/fg-line-sync/full-r28.
not_allowed: no rule or constant per case / kernel / shape / library; no constant chosen by full-GPU error; the criteria above may be relaxed only in an addendum that says why and whether the data had been seen; cells that fail and counter-examples stay in the report.

addenda.hypothesis_for_run_3 (post hoc, from rea: the measured kernel of FIF-RMSNORM carries ACQBULK as its fifth instruction and PREEXIT before EXIT; the probe has neither. Of the 500 b300 full-GPU cases, the measured kernel has ACQBULK in 139; among launches with more than 1.5 waves the ones the simulation runs fastest are ACQBULK kernels with short CTAs (FIF-RMSNORM x4 0.69-0.76, FIF-CLASSIC-SILU-AND-MUL-E02 0.78, DGF-HC-PRENORM x5 0.80-0.89), while CUF-DSL-RMSNORM (same DSL, same prologue without ACQBULK, 6.9 waves) is at 0.89-1.03. ACQBULK / PREEXIT are assumed to be what ptxas emits for griddepcontrol.wait / griddepcontrol.launch_dependents (programmatic dependent launch); run 3's SASS check decides that assumption first.
addenda.cells_G: probe option --pdl (bit 0 griddepcontrol.wait after the first clock read, bit 1 griddepcontrol.launch_dependents as the last instruction). Without ncu, 5 launches: rms.t128.g8192.h1400 with pdl 0 / 1 / 2 / 3; rms.t128.g5612.h1400 and g7552 with pdl 3; spin.t128.o0.w6.h2200.j150 with pdl 3. Under ncu --cache-control all, 3 launches, the cells-F metric list: rms.t128.g8192.h1400 with pdl 3 and pdl 0.
addenda.prediction: SASS: ACQBULK appears iff bit 0, PREEXIT iff bit 1 (if not, the assumption is wrong and the cells only say that these PTX instructions do not matter). If these instructions are what the replica lacked: the cells with the responsible bit have span / M2-replay >= 1.25 (as a longer gap, or as a residency the counters would not see) and pdl 0 stays <= 1.05; the grid 5612 / 7552 / 8192 cells then show the reference's uneven growth (13.8 / 17.1 / 19.7 k: +1.69 then +4.09 cycles per added CTA). If every cell is <= 1.05 the hypothesis is refuted and the excess stays open. Nothing is installed from cells G; a positive result is reported to the user with the dependence table before any engine rule (it would need a mechanism of its own).

reading_of_run_3.SASS: the binary with the two PTX instructions has exactly one ACQBULK (right after the first clock reads, i.e. griddepcontrol.wait) and one PREEXIT (before the last EXIT, i.e. griddepcontrol.launch_dependents) on both devices; the run-1 / run-2 binaries had neither. One binary serves all cells, so 'iff bit' is read from the position of the instructions, not per cell.
reading_of_run_3.which bit: bit 0 (ACQBULK executed) changes nothing: rms grid 8192 span / M2-replay 1.026 (b300) / 1.018 (h100) against 1.025 / 1.022 with neither. addenda.cells_P (one card, one job): spin.t128.o0.w12.h3000.j300 first and last; cpasync, ldg at hold 3000 (12 waves); rms at hold 1400 with the grid of 12 waves; cpasync with --mem-permille 250 / 500; cpasync at hold 6000.
addenda.predictions for cells P: the spin cell shows four slow gpcs (150-182 / 240-274 ns on b300, about 147-162 / 172-196 ns on h100), the same four in its repetition. If the rise of the slow class belongs to the cell kind, cpasync and ldg show it on this card (b300 slow class above 650 cycles) and rms does not; if it belongs to the card, all three agree. If it follows the read traffic, the 250 / 500 permille cells lie between the spin and the full value in that order; the hold-6000 cell says whether it needs the read to be recent.
addenda.what gets installed for the gpc classes: decided after run 4 in an addendum. Known constraint: which gpcs are slow is a property of the card, not of the device, and the reference card of a case is not recorded; a per-gpc leaf can therefore fix the two class values and the number of slow gpcs but only a declared choice of which ones.

addenda.written: after run 4 on both devices ($A/fg-line-cold/refill/{b300,h100}-r4; model output $A/fg-line-cold/refill-model/{b300,h100}-r4{.tsv,/model4.json}, gpc_classes.json; tools/gpc_classes.py). b300 r4 ran on the card of r1 (GPU-36989eed), h100 r4 on a fourth card.

reading_of_run_4.PREEXIT, M3a: holds. Replay on the measured residencies with the cell's own PREEXIT mask, u = 1.00 (b300) / 0.95 (h100) as fitted on the one run-3 cell: span / M3a 0.980-1.005 on 17 of the 18 cells G on b300 and 0.975-1.023 on all 18 on h100. Per CTA, not per warp: 1 or 2 of the 4 warps executing give the span of all four (b300 29769 / 29822 against 29762, h100 30184 / 30194 against 30159) -> M3b refuted; 8-warp CTAs cost one unit as well (span / M3a 1.001 / 0.990), 1-warp CTAs too (0.999 / 1.002). Linear in the fraction of CTAs: 0 / 250 / 500 / 750 / 1000 permille -> 19.1 / 20.7 / 23.7 / 26.8 / 29.8 k (b300), 18.8 / 21.0 / 23.9 / 27.0 / 30.2 k (h100) -> M3c refuted. Executing it right after entry instead of before exit: 29471 / 30004. The launch attribute changes nothing: with it and PREEXIT 29820 / 30198, with it and no PREEXIT 19069 / 18807.
reading_of_run_4.counter-example: b300, 512-thread CTAs (4 slots per SM, 16 warps) with PREEXIT: span / M3a 1.050 (h100 1.023). The launch is not serial-limited (0.34 CTAs per cycle); the steady gap of the fast SM class rises from 313 to about 470-500 cycles, the slow class stays (516 -> 535). Not explained, not modelled; the 5 % criterion fails on this one cell, so b300 is installed as experimental.
reading_of_run_4.gpc classes: confirmed on a fourth card per device: four whole topology gpcs are slow, the others (and on b300 the six SMs without a gpc id) fast; the same four in the first and last cell of the job. Class values over the six spin cells of runs 1, 2, 4 (per-SM median steady gap, generations >= 5, converted with each cell's cycles per ns): b300 fast 159.4 ns (154.0-170.9), slow 250.9 ns (245.1-262.3); h100 fast 150.3 ns (147.0-154.7), slow 183.5 ns (180.5-187.7). Which four: b300 {2,5,6,7} on two cards (r1 = r4, r3), {1,2,6,7} on one (r2); h100 {1,2,3,7} on three cards, {1,2,3,5} on one.
reading_of_run_4.M4 (not declared before run 4): M3a with the class value of each SM: span / M4 0.986-1.022 on the 16 run-4 cells replayed on b300 (512-thread PREEXIT cell 1.063), 0.976-1.029 on h100. On these uniform probes a single mean constant does as well (M3a column); the class rule is installed because it is what the hardware does, not because the span needs it.
reading_of_run_4.what the slow class depends on (cells P,: the rise to about 685 cycles appears with cold global reads in every CTA at a constant hold of 3000 (cpasync 684, ldg 685; fast class 320 unchanged) and at hold 0 (slow 788, fast 332-502 by gpc), and does not appear at hold 6000 (500), with 25 % or 50 % of the CTAs reading (500 / 500), or in the kernel-shaped cell (505). h100 shows none in any cell. Prediction 'follows the read traffic in order' refuted; no rule is derived from it.

installed.engine: a CTA in which PREEXIT was executed occupies the GPU-wide dispatch serializer for dependents_launch_serial_ns at its completion; a slot is placeable slot_free_to_entry_ns after its CTA's completion on SMs whose topology gpc is not in slow_gpc_mask and slot_free_to_entry_slow_ns on the others.
installed.b300: slot_free_to_entry_ns 159.4, slot_free_to_entry_slow_ns 250.9, slow_gpc_mask {2,5,6,7}, dependents_launch_serial_ns 0.513613 (1.00 x serial_ns_per_cta); all experimental.
installed.h100: slot_free_to_entry_ns 150.3 (was 174.924), slot_free_to_entry_slow_ns 183.5, slow_gpc_mask {1,2,3,7}, dependents_launch_serial_ns 0.586 (0.95 x 0.617); experimental.
installed.declared choice: slow_gpc_mask is the set seen on most of the cards measured (2 of 3, 3 of 4). The card a reference was taken on is not recorded, and whether the set differs by card or the SM numbering differs by card is not separated.

addenda.not_modelled: first-wave spread; the rise of the b300 slow class under the two conditions above; the 16-warp PREEXIT cell; the longer gap after nanosleep holds.
